commands.name: import_commit
commands.behavior: Commit a staged import: copy/move/reference only the `selected` source files, then apply `options` to the freshly-added rows. Emits `import:progress` (live rows) + `import:done`.  `pairing` decides what happens to a JPEG/HEIF the camera wrote beside a RAW: `"pair"` links it to that RAW (one grid cell), anything else (the default) catalogs every file standalone.  The run is non-durable and cancellable between 16-file chunks: an interrupted run keeps every committed row and still reports it (`import:done` payload gains `interrupted` and `notProcessed` = selected files never reached). Every catalog write is fenced on the catalog epoch the run started under — on a stale catalog nothing further is written and source originals are never trashed.
commands.test: crates/core-import/tests/import_copy.rs

commands.name: hdr_merge
commands.behavior: Single-flight merge 2–9 unique bracket frames into HDR EXR; publish via synced unique temporary file without overwrite, remove output on cancellation or catalog failure, emit progress and completion.  Source publication tokens are captured only after validation, and the provenance insert runs under `tokens_guard`: if a source changed mid-merge its output is removed and nothing is published; a result committed before cancellation survives and the job reports `Interrupted`.
commands.test: crates/core-runtime/tests/publication.rs

commands.name: hdr_cancel
commands.behavior: Request the running HDR merge to stop (honored between frames). No-op if idle.

commands.name: analysis_run
commands.behavior: Run the background analysis pass. `force` re-analyzes everything. Emits `analysis:progress`/`:done`.  `scope` narrows the pass to the container the grid is showing. The frontend may post its whole filter — `ScanScope` deserializes only the container dimensions, so rating/flag/search and the scan-derived `detectedCategory`/`personId` are dropped by the type. Omitted ⇒ whole library.  Legacy entry point: it runs every AI stage. The Run-AI-scan modal calls `scan_run` instead, which owns stage selection and sequences panorama detection in the same job.
